articles.title: Sandra Wollner’s ‘Everytime’ Is a Stunning Film About Grief Like You’ve Never Seen Before
articles.summary: The German filmmaker's portrait of life after tragedy is filled with the unexpected. She tells IndieWire about video game cut scenes, the power of banal memories, the scene that makes everyone gasp, and what it all means. Sort of.
articles.content: Few human emotions are as fathomable as grief. Someone (or something) was here, had meaning and value and presence, and is now gone. There is a hole, a gap, an empty space. The pain that accompanies that void may manifest in different people in different ways, but its very existence is understandable. What makes people happy? What makes them sad? What makes them angry? Grief, well, that’s an easier question with a tougher answer. For her third feature film , German filmmaker Sandra Wollner tackles the most tangible of dramatic genres — the grief tale — and turns it on its head in a way that our own David Ehrlich called “infinitely beguiling.” Mostly, the film shows how infinitely elastic and malleable this genre is, and the emotions that power it. articles.title: DC Studios’ Latest Reboot: James Gunn and Peter Safran’s Exit Is About Cost-Cutting, Not Just Creative Issues
articles.summary: The pair signed a very generous deal with David Zaslav. Jeremy Latcham will be a lot cheaper.
articles.content: When they were hired to run DC Studios , James Gunn and Peter Safran were tasked with turning the struggling comic book company into a true rival to Marvel. Four years later, the two have been handed their walking papers before they were able to accomplish their task. Skydance , which recently bought Warner Bros. Discovery and with it the rights to heroes like Superman, Batman, and the other DC staples that Gunn and Safran were trying to reinvigorate, opted to go in another, cheaper direction. They brought in Jeremy Latcham, a low-profile executive who, like Gunn, had spent years working for Marvel, to oversee DC’s latest reboot. Related Stories ‘Paper Tiger’ Review: Adam Driver Gives a Career-Best Performance in James Gray’s Devastating Tragedy ‘Iron Boy’ Trailer: Beloved Animated Feature Oscar Contender Throws a Whole Watercolor World Out of Whack There have been mutterings that the change was because of the commercial performance of DC’s films, and the track record has been a mixed bag. “Superman” did what it needed to do, earning $618.7 million worldwide on a $225 million budget, but it wasn’t a blockbuster on the level of Christopher Nolan’s “Dark Knight” films or “Aquaman.” But “Supergirl” was an unmitigated disaster , earning $126.5 million against a $170 million budget, resulting in losses of roughly $100 million. And “Clayface,” a body horror film produced for $44 million, has been a modest success, earning approximately $110 million. So no, Gunn and Safran had yet to produce a “Guardians of the Galaxy”-style smash that taps the zeitgeist. Though, to be fair, Marvel hasn’t made as many of those lately either. Tastes have changed, and comic book movies, at least ones not starring Spider-Man , aren’t as popular as they once were. But look closer, and Gunn and Safran’s ouster is about something more than their films’ commercial performances. It’s about cost-cutting too, something that Skydance, with its $80 billion in net debt, needs to start chipping away at

articles.content: Frank Grillo took to social media to express all of his gratitude to former DC Studios co-heads James Gunn and Peter Safran . Following the merger of Warner Bros. and Paramount, Skydance parted ways with Gunn and Safran, who were still in the initial stages of rebuilding the DC Universe. Amid the executive shakeup , Grillo posted a video with a message to the departing duo. “I feel like now that the dust has settled a bit, and every jerk off with an Instagram handle has an opinion — I just wanted to publicly thank two of the finest men that I’ve met in this business, in Peter Safran and James Gunn,” Grillo said on Instagram. “Two of the most loyal guys. It traces how jazz took root in Japan and how a new generation is reshaping it. The crew also drops in on Masako, a Shimokitazawa jazz café now in the hands of a third generation, and on No Room for Squares, which Nakata Kohei founded. Gentle Forest Jazz Band and GCR Orchestra also appear. “Tokyo is a city that never really slows down, but you can step into a small room where everyone has come for one reason: to listen,” said Srivastava. “Outside those rooms, you meet musicians taking jazz in completely new directions. I wanted this film to bring both worlds together. That’s the Tokyo I found most interesting.” A first round of filming in Japan has already been completed, and the team has put together a short-form version from that material. A teaser is also out. Production will return to Tokyo April 1–22, 2027, for the final shoot, with completion targeted for June that year. articles.content: Russell Brand , who was convicted of rape last week in London, posted on X Wednesday that his Instagram account has been removed by Meta. Brand posted a screenshot reading, “We disabled your account. Our technology found your account, or your activity on it, doesn’t follow our rules.” “We suspended your page. Brand’s X page, with 10 million followers, is still active. “There never was a Russell Brand, according to @Meta . Thank God for @elonmusk . Stay tuned,” he wrote on X Wednesday. Brand’s account was taken down because it “violates our policies,” a Meta spokesperson confirmed to TMZ . After Brand’s comedy and movie appearances tapered off, he started a YouTube channel which during the COVID pandemic became increasingly right-wing and full of conspiracy theories. He was accused of sexual misconduct multiple times before finally being charged in 2025. In 2023, YouTube suspended monetization of his account. Judge Joel Bennathan began his sentencing remarks Monday by saying, “About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous. You were clever and, in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic. articles.title: Randall England, ‘General Hospital’ Star, Dies at 75
articles.content: Randall England , an actor, model, writer and producer who appeared in TV shows including “ General Hospital ,” died Sept. 25 in Los Angeles, his family has announced. He was 75. England began his career in 1978 with an uncredited role in the TV movie “Ruby and Oswalk” before landing an episode of the TV series “This Is the Life” in 1984. That same year, England was cast as “General Hospital” villain Jack Slater, and went on to appear on more than 30 episodes of the long-running soap opera. He appeared in two episodes of “Baywatch” in the late 1990s, and also voiced the character of Butler in the 2008 film “Beverly Hills Chihuahua.” Related Stories Why Does Amazon Want a TV Show Starring Melania Trump? Oscar Predictions: Best Actor — The Most Competitive Acting Category Has a Deep Bench of Contenders His last credit was for the 2018 film “Shiner,” and his producing work included the documentary The Needs of Kim Stanley. On stage, England appeared in productions of “All My Sons,” “The Glass Menagerie” and “The Three Sisters,” the latter of which he won a Drama League Award for best ensemble cast. England was born on September 22, 1951, in Oklahoma City and graduated from the University of Oklahoma. He began modeling in the early 1970s and went on to work in New York, London, Zurich, Milan and Los Angeles. He studied acting with Kim Stanley and Stella Adler before building a career across television, film and theater. He is survived by daughter Micaela Reed (Sam); grandchildren Katherine and Julian; mother Catherine Burgess; sister Linda Baker; and extended family. While England’s family did not confirm his cause of death, they noted that memorial donations can be made to the Esophageal Cancer Action Network (ECAN).

Kimmel also did well in terms of rating among adults age 18-49, scoring a 0.32 — an increase of 68% from 2022’s 0.19 rating. Excluding episodes that benefited from NFL, NBA and NHL lead-in, that’s the highest rating Kimmel has seen in more than a year, since the buzzy episode on Sept. 23, 2025 in which he returned to the air after his controversial suspension over comments he made about the assassination of Charlie Kirk. The season average to date is 2.5 million viewers, up 16% from last year’s 2.1 million viewer-average at the same point in time. Season 25 is currently on track to become Kimmel’s most-watched in 12 years, since the 2014-2015 season.

articles.title: Snoop Dogg Sets NBC Holiday Special ‘Christmas With Snoop’
articles.content: Snoop Dogg will celebrate the holiday season with an NBC special “Christmas With Snoop,” airing on the network on Dec. 2 at 10 p.m. and streaming the next day on Peacock. The broadcast will find the gangsta rapper turned cuddly corporate mascot posting up in a plush hotel suite, partying with his friends and loved ones. The holiday special will feature appearances and musical performances from Wayne Brady, Kristin Chenoweth, Adam Devine, Anelise Foxx, Jamie Foxx, Jane Handcock, October London, Craig Robinson, Nicole Scherzinger, Gwen Stefani and, obviously, Martha Stewart, who has formed an unlikely friendship with Snoop Dogg and, over the years, featured him on her cooking programs. Related Stories Oscars: International Feature — ‘La Bola Negra,’ ‘Fjord’ and 'Minotaur' Lead Early Contenders Oscar Predictions: Best Adapted Screenplay — Epics, Trilogies and a Wild Dinner Party Could Define the Race The “Gin and Juice” icon goes way back with NBC, recently serving as an Olympics correspondent. He appeared on TV offering commentary at the 2021 Tokyo games as well as Paris in 2024 and Milan-Cortina in 2026. A couple of years ago, Snoop Dogg also served as a judge on the NBC singing competition program “The Voice,” returning for another season in 2025. Also in 2025, Snoop Dogg and his production company, Death Row Pictures, signed a multi-year, first-look creative partnership with NBCUniversal spanning film, television, sports entertainment and streaming. And Universal Pictures is releasing a Snoop Dogg biopic in August 2027, with Jonathan Daviss playing the hip-hop legend. “Christmas with Snoop” is executive produced by Snoop Dogg and Sara Ramaker for Death Row Pictures along with Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay for Jesse Collins Entertainment. The special hails from NBCUniversal.

articles.title: How KROQ’s ‘Klein/Ally Show’ Slogged Its Way to the Top in Los Angeles Radio Morning Drive
articles.content: As KROQ gets ready to hold the 35th edition of its “Almost Acoustic Christmas” concert event next month, the “world famous” alternative rock station has even more reason to celebrate: Not only did the station hit its best ratings in September since Summer 2004, but KROQ is once again a force in Los Angeles morning drive radio. Variety noted last year that KROQ has been on a comeback ever since the returns of longtime program director Kevin Weatherly in June 2022 and former morning show host Kevin Ryder, who was given the afternoon drive-time slot in April 2025. But the rebirth of KROQ can also be attributed to the massive growth of “Klein.Ally.Show” in the mornings, which has seen a remarkable rise, particularly over the past year. articles.title: Nicole Kidman to Receive Honorary Cesar Award From French Film Academy
articles.summary: The French Academy paid tribute to the 'Moulin Rouge!,' 'Eyes Wide Shut' and 'Practical Magic' actress, saying Kidman "has never allowed her status as a star to dictate her artistic choices."
articles.content: Nicole Kidman will receive an honorary César, the highest award in French cinema, from the French film academy, the Académie des Arts et Techniques du Cinéma. The Oscar-winning actress will be honored for her life’s work at the 2027 César awards in Paris in February. Announcing the honor on Thursday, the Académie called Kidman both “a Hollywood star and a major figure in auteur cinema,” saying the Australian actress “has built a career that defies categorization.” Related Stories Movies 'Russell Brand: Open Secret' Documentary Set at Netflix Movies Golshifteh Farahani Is a Widow Fighting the Exploitation of Kids as the Taliban Nears Kabul in 'When She Hears the Bells' (Exclusive Clip and Chat) Kidman is among a handful of actors who have achieved success both with studio blockbusters, in films such as Aquaman and Pratical Magic , and with art-house features, in her work with the likes of Stanley Kubrick ( Eyes Wide Shut ), Jane Campion ( The Portrait of a Lady ), Lars von Trier ( Dogville ), and Baz Luhrmann ( Moulin Rouge! ). A five-time Oscar nominee, she won the Academy Award for Best Actress in 2003 for her portrayal of Virginia Woolf in Stephen Daldry’s The Hours . More recently, Kidman received the Volpi Cup for Best Actress at the 2024 Venice Film Festival for her role in Halina Reijn’s Babygirl . Also a producer, Kidman, through her Blossom Films shingle, has produced, and starred in, such series as Big Little Lies , The Undoing , and Nine Perfect Strangers . With the honorary César, the French Academy said it wishes “to pay tribute to an actress and producer who has never allowed her status as a star to dictate her artistic choices.” In recent years, the Césars have singled out Hollywood talent for their honorary award. Last year’s honoree was Jim Carrey and recent recipients include Julia Roberts , Christopher Nolan, David Fincher and Cate Blanchett . articles.title: ‘Russell Brand: Open Secret’ Documentary Set at Netflix
articles.summary: From the producers of 'Jimmy Savile: A British Horror Story,' the film promises to examine Brand's journey from superstar to convicted rapist.
articles.content: A Russell Brand documentary is coming to Netflix, set to chart his comedy stardom to a criminal trial that culminated in a 10-year prison sentence for rape and sexual assault this week. Russell Brand: Open Secret is from the producers of Jimmy Savile: A British Horror Story , 72 Films, a Fremantle company, and directed by Olivia Isaacs. The doc promises to feature inside voices and archive footage, providing insight into Brand’s life and the investigation that started it all at The Times and The Sunday Times , through their chief news correspondent, Rosamund Urwin and investigations correspondent, Charlotte Wace. Crucially, Russell Brand: Open Secret will examine how, despite many people in the TV industry being aware of his behavior, he evaded punishment for so long. Related Stories Movies China's Film Industry Arrives at AFM on a Domestic High Movies Can Constantin Survive Its Own Parent Company? Brand’s four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court captivated the country and British media. After being sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on Monday, the disgraced star was led away and transferred to HMP Wandsworth prison. He’ll be expected to serve around seven years of that prison sentence before being released on licence. The judge, Justice Bennathan, took Brand through all of his crimes in extensive detail, citing the witness impact statements from the four victims before handing down the sentence. He said Brand operated with “staggering arrogance” during the attacks and that his entourage often “indulged” his “dreadful behavior.” He said toward the end of his statement: “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say ‘no’ and to demand justice from criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent.” Among the crimes he was convicted of were a violent anal rape of a woman at his Hampstead home in 2009 and three sexual assaults.

articles.summary: Chabname Zariab’s Tallinn-debuting debut feature includes images shot in Afghanistan and shines a light on women and a "taboo" topic in a story that is "a personal responsibility and an act of quiet resistance."
articles.content: Golshifteh Farahani ‘s ( Alpha , Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales , The Pear Tree ) new film, writer-director Chabname Zariab’s debut feature When She Hears the Bells (Les Clochettes de Kaboul) , is both a thriller and a call to stand up for human rights. France-based Iranian actress Farahani stars as Leila, a young widow seeking a fresh start in Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan. But she soon finds out that the kitchen, in which she finds work, is a so-called bacha bazi house. These are establishments in which boys and young men are forced to dress in women’s clothes and dance for entertainment – and for sexual and other exploitation. At the same time – it is 2021 – the Taliban is moving closer and closer to Kabul. Leila tries to flee and also help a group of boys escape before the city falls. Sayed Hashimi ( 13 Days, 13 Nights ) co-stars in the film, which includes images actually shot in Afghanistan. Pierre Cottereau handled cinematography, while the editors are Xavier Sirven, Héloïse Pelloquet and Julie Duclaux. articles.title: Compassion and Bureaucracy Clash in ‘A Job Well Done,’ Which Explores Immigration Through Social Workers’ Eyes
articles.summary: Fred Baillif's new film, premiering in the main competition at Tallinn, mixes fiction and documentary elements to talk about "how we in the Western world see the 'useful' and the 'useless' migrants."
articles.content: What do you do when the only way to help someone is to break the rules and the law? This clash between compassion and solidarity on the one side and the legal framework on the other is at the heart of A Job Well Done ( Un travail exemplaire ), the new feature blending fiction and documentary from Swiss writer-director Fred Baillif , which dives into the complexities and moral ambiguity that social workers face. In his work, the former national basketball player and prison educator draws on his background in social work to make films that are rooted in real life and explore contradictions that people working on the tricky frontlines of social services. He previously put a spotlight on street work in Tapis rouge and life in a group home in The Fam ( La Mif ). Related Stories Movies "I Look Good With a Weapon in My Hand": Priyanka Chopra Jonas on Trading Weapons for Words in 'Bluefly' Movies China's Film Industry Arrives at AFM on a Domestic High In A Job Well Done , Baillif takes us inside a double-decker bus in Geneva, where social workers welcome migrants who are looking for help, a shelter, or simply someone to talk to. On this frontline of Switzerland’s asylum system, the desire to help refugees means navigating an increasingly Kafkaesque bureaucracy. “Behind every file, a life is told: a young woman in conflict with her family, an asylum seeker facing deportation, homeless people, a woman trying to escape violence,” reads a synopsis on the PÖFF website. “The team looks for solutions, negotiates, insists. But places are scarce, procedures run their course, and institutional responses collide with the urgency of the situations. Among colleagues, convictions clash: keep within the framework to preserve the welcome, or step outside it rather than abandon someone?” The film will have its world premiere on Nov. 14 in the Official Selection Competition at the the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia. articles.title: “I Look Good With a Weapon in My Hand”: Priyanka Chopra Jonas on Trading Weapons for Words in ‘Bluefly’
articles.summary: Playing a U.N. interpreter who’d rather avoid conflict, the action regular says she’s excited to dig into the dramatic side of a character, alongside Russell Crowe.
articles.content: Priyanka Chopra Jonas has had her fair share of action roles. From Citadel to The Bluff , the actress is rarely seen onscreen without a firearm. But for her upcoming role in the sci-fi action thriller Bluefly , also starring Russell Crowe , Chopra Jonas has found a new weapon: language. She stars as U.N. interpreter Myla Reese, who joins Crowe’s Benny on a covert mission in the Congo, where they become privy to a powerful force hidden deep within the jungle. Related Stories Movies A Rom-Com Connoisseur Goes Into Business With the True Story of a Sex Toy Saleswoman Movies China's Film Industry Arrives at AFM on a Domestic High With the action secondary, Chopra Jonas is focused on bringing “a certain softness” to the film rather than being the one who takes charge and wields the weapons. And after 15 years of working with UNICEF, she feels a great responsibility to properly portray a U.N. interpreter. “I’m working with my dialect coach to get the words right in the multiple African languages I’m going to attempt, from Swahili to Zulu to Lingala,” she says. Highland Film Group is handling worldwide rights on the film, which is directed by Nimród Antal and written by David Frigerio, William Eubank and Carlyle Eubank. Days before cameras rolled in Australia, Chopra Jonas spoke with THR about what attracted her to Bluefly , working with Crowe and why she’s a big fan of movie magic. articles.title: ‘Wet,’ Starring Connor Storrie, Rebecca Ferguson and Odessa A’zion, Acquired by Lionsgate
articles.summary: Javier Bardem, Rosalía and Lukas Haas are also starring in the film from director Alma Har’el.
articles.content: Lionsgate has acquired the North America and U.K. distribution rights for Wet from director Alma Har’el ( Honey Boy , Lady in the Lake ), The Hollywood Reporter has learned. The film, produced by Fifth Season and 193, a Legendary Company, is set to star Connor Storrie ( Heated Rivalry ), Rebecca Ferguson ( Dune and Silo ), Odessa A’zion ( Marty Supreme ), Javier Bardem ( Biutiful and Dune ), Rosalía ( Euphoria ) and Lukas Haas ( Spider-Noir ). Har’el co-wrote the screenplay with Christian Stangeby, though the plotline is being kept under wraps. I’m grateful to Lionsgate for embracing a film that speaks to this wild moment in time. Har’el, Christopher Leggett and Riva Marker are serving as producers for Linden Entertainment, while Christopher Slager and Graham Taylor are executive producing with Patrick Wachsberger and Ashley Stern for 193. articles.title: ‘One in a Million’ Filmmaker on the Ethical Dilemma He Faced and Learning to Let His Subject Find Her Own Way
articles.summary: Over a decade, co-directors Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes documented a young Syrian girl named Israa and her family's changing dynamics as refugees in Germany.
articles.content: For One in a Million filmmakers Jack MacInnes and Itab Azzam, documenting the life of a Syrian refugee family for more than a decade meant confronting a complicated question: What’s the line between documenting the truth and protecting your subject? That conundrum came to a head when a 14-year-old girl named Israa, whom the married documentarians had been following since the age of 11, when her parents decided to immigrate from Turkey to Germany, revealed that her father, Tarek, had hit her. articles.summary: Revenue still trails last year’s 'Ne Zha 2'-fueled peak, but homegrown hits are driving the 2026 box office and the industry is courting partners abroad.
articles.content: Chinese filmmaker Wen Muye keeps taking what look on paper like challenging subjects and turning them into box office gold. It began with his 2018 debut, Dying to Survive , about a man (Xu Zheng) who makes a fortune smuggling cancer drugs into China . The film took in more than $450 million, and Wen was hailed as an exciting new voice in Chinese cinema. He blended so much humanity and humor into the story that, by the time the credits rolled, the film had become the tale of a man who went looking for cash but found his soul. When news of Wen’s latest venture broke, Chinese media initially struggled with what they’d heard of Once Upon a Time in the Middle East : the fact that it would be set in the war-torn Middle East, inside a Chinese restaurant, and would star one of the country’s most beloved comedians in Shen Teng ( Pegasus ) led to some head scratching. articles.summary: Jordan Firstman, Matteo Lane, Nicole Byer and John Cameron Mitchell lead the English voice cast of the adult animated comedy about a mysterious virus turning gay men straight.

articles.summary: Paolo Strippoli’s acclaimed horror-thriller stars Jasmine Trinca as a mother drawn into a Faustian pact with a mysterious stranger played by Valeria Bruni Tedeschi.
articles.content: Le Pacte has secured a North American distribution deal and a raft of international sales for Paolo Strippoli’s horror-thriller The Spiral , which premiered to strong reviews in Venice and later became Italy’s submission for the best international feature Oscar. The North American deal includes a commitment to a U.S. theatrical release. The distributor’s identity will be announced at a later date, with Le Pacte saying that the agreement could be extended to additional territories. Vertigo Releasing acquired the film for the U.K. and Ireland, MFA+ FilmDistribution took Germany, Austria and Switzerland, and La Aventura Cine picked up Spain. Other European buyers include Aurora Films for Poland, Pris Audiovisuais for Portugal, ABCinema for Greece, Independenta Film for Romania, MCF Megacom Film for the Balkans, Bestfilm.eu for the Baltics and Beta Film for Bulgaria. articles.content: Anthony Clark, the stand-up comedian best known for playing Greg Warner on the CBS sitcom Yes, Dear , has died. He was 62. articles.title: Randall England, ‘General Hospital’ Actor, Dies at 75
articles.summary: He played the villainous Jack Slater on the ABC soap opera and, later, Bill Clinton on the stage.
articles.content: Randall England, who portrayed Jack Slater, a villain fond of red cowboy boots, for eight months in the mid-1980s on the ABC soap General Hospital , has died. He was 75. England died Sept. 25 after a battle with esophageal cancer, his family announced . He lived in Beverly Hills for more than 40 years, and the town “won’t be the same without him cruising around in his vintage BMW, sporting his dark Ray-Ban sunglasses,” they noted. From November 1984 through June 1985, England played Slater, a killer and jewel thief who went toe-to-toe with Tristan Rogers ’ Robert Scorpio before he’s shot to death. (It turns out he was a fan of cowboy boots in real life.) Related Stories Movies Irma P. Hall, Actress in 'Soul Food' and 'The Ladykillers,' Dies at 91 Movies Stacy Keach, Who Played Badasses With the Best of Them, Dies at 85 One of three kids, Randy Alan England was born in Oklahoma City on Sept. 22, 1951. He graduated from Memorial High School and the University of Oklahoma, where he was a pitcher for the Sooners. After working as a model on gigs that took him to London, Zurich, Milan and Los Angeles, he studied acting in the late 1970s and early ’80s with Kim Stanley and Stella Adler. An audition brought him to L.A., and in 1981 he showed up as a model in the Michael Crichton thriller Looker , starring Albert Finney . England also appeared on episodes of Dallas , The Young and the Restless and Baywatch and in the 2015 music video for Maroon 5’s “Sugar.” For the stage, he played President Clinton in Hillary & Monica in 2003 in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and acted in productions of All My Sons , The Glass Menagerie and Three Sisters . He was working on documentary that honored Stanley’s life and career and the time of his death. Survivors include his daughter, Micaela, and son-in-law, Sam; his grandchildren, Katherine and Julian; his mother, Catherine; sister Linda; nieces and nephews Amanda, Wesley and Alex; and ex-wife Jennifer.

articles.content: In a strange move, Kurt Wimmer and Leslie Dixon will get screenplay credit despite not working on the new version of the movie at all Michael B. Jordan’s “Thomas Crown Affair” may be a fresh take on the classic heist story, but its writing credits reach back to an earlier incarnation. TheWrap has learned that Kurt Wimmer and Leslie Dixon, who wrote the 1999 remake, will receive screenplay credit alongside Drew Pearce. The new film, starring and directed by Jordan, is set to hit theaters March 5, 2027, courtesy of Amazon MGM Studios. The story first hit the screen in 1968, starring Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway. The 1999 remake swapped in Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo, with Wimmer and Dixon handling the screenplay. Alan Trustman, who wrote the original film, will receive a “story by” credit on the new version alongside Joe Carnahan, who wrote an earlier draft. What makes this credit so strange – bordering on unprecedented – is the fact that Dixon and Wimmer had nothing to do with this reimagined version. But the Writers Guild of America still awarded them screenplay credit. You would imagine that they would have received story by credit, alongside Trustman, but they are getting full screenplay credit, next to Pearce. The credits will make their debut in a trailer and poster for 2027’s “Thomas Crown Affair,” set to be released later this week. There are occasionally instances of the original writer being credited on remakes even if they had nothing to do with the newer version – while John Hughes wrote the script for 1997’s “Flubber,” he shared the credit with original “Absent-Minded Professor” writer Bill Walsh, even though he died in 1975. articles.title: Attend, the First Marketplace Connecting Filmmakers Directly to Theater Owners, Finally Launches Today
articles.summary: IndieWire got a first look at The Fithian Group's long-awaited portal ahead of its debut at the American Film Market.
articles.content: Way back in October 2024, The Fithian Group, led by former NATO chief John Fithian and founding partner Patrick Corcoran, announced plans for an ambitious new marketplace , one that would help connect filmmakers and their projects directly to theater owners looking to book their movies and effectively cut out the distribution middleman. Today, that vision is now a reality. The Fithian Group on Wednesday at the American Film Market announced the formal launch of Attend Theatrical Marketplace, the group’s online platform and marketplace for filmmakers and exhibitors that is now live and ready for business. Attend launches with today just a curated selection of four films, all of whose filmmakers will now be doing the legwork to connect with theaters and find venues at which to exhibit their work. But the platform is already loaded with exhibition partners who will be able to browse available films, with more to be added soon, and Attend will eventually be a fully open platform to any filmmaker who wishes to do outreach directly to theater owners. articles.content: Can a conservative “canceled” theater director rise from the ashes of his own ruination — and in this climate ? That’s one of the questions top of mind for filmmakers Nicholas Clark and Dylan Frederick, whose provocative, Christopher Guest-style nonfiction film “American Theater” (except it’s a docu -, not mocku mentary) is rolling out in select theaters now. A Slamdance Grand Jury Prize winner for documentary in 2025, the film is also executive-produced by Jeremy O. Harris . “American Theater” follows Brian Clowdus — openly gay, conservative, and formerly of the Serenbe Playhouse in Georgia, who was taken down in 2019 over allegations of racism, misconduct, unsafe working conditions, and a gamut of other accusations. Clark and Frederick follow Clowdus, now a MAGA Republican, and a troupe of other conservative actors to an abandoned cabin in middle-of-nowhere Georgia where Clowdus plots the ultimate revenge: a community musical theater retelling of, of course, the 1692 Salem witch trials, riffing on Arthur Miller’s “The Crucible” (which, published in 1953, isn’t yet in the public domain). articles.title: Fan Edits Are Legal with Moonbeem, Distribution Network Hosts Approved Clips from Filmmakers
articles.summary: Exclusive: The company, which was incubated by the Sundance Institute, unveils its free panel for Adobe Premiere Pro.
articles.content: Film lovers can make and post their fan edits legally thanks to Moonbeem , a distribution network for independent film. Fan edits are among the most-watched film content on social media, and nearly all of them are made from footage whose rights nobody cleared. But on Moonbeem, the rights holder decides which scenes to open and creators cut from those scenes. Moreover, every fan edit points viewers back to where the film can be rented, bought, or watched. Fan edits made this way have been viewed more than 190 million times across the network. The company has unveiled its free panel for Adobe Premiere Pro, which is where the approved scenes will be available. The announcement comes during Adobe MAX, the tech company’s annual conference in Miami Beach, Florida. The company believes it’s one of the first times fans can cut real scenes from released films, with the rights holders’ permission, in the editing software they already use. articles.title: ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Review: David Leitch’s Fun and Poppy YouTube Heist Movie Almost Gets Away with It
articles.summary: Nicholas Hoult plays a live-streaming Robin Hood in an "eat the rich" thriller funded by Jeff Bezos.
articles.content: The major Hollywood studios tend to shy away from the subject of class warfare because they know they can’t pull them off with a straight face. But young people in this country are increasingly animated by radical leftist ideas like “earning a livable wage” and “being able to buy a home before they die,” and at a certain point the movies will have to meet them where they live. Perhaps that point is now. How else to explain why Jeff Bezos would fund a Robin Hood-esque heist thriller that not only encourages its target demographic to commit armed robberies, but also kinda sorta teaches them how? (No one is going to confuse a David Leitch movie for “The Anarchist Cookbook.”) At a time when internet activists like Hasan Piker have come to occupy more space in the public imagination than Marvel superheroes, selling the masses on fanciful stories about the downward redistribution of wealth might be the billionaire class’ best protection against the threat of it actually happening in real life. It’s a lot more fun than paying a proportional tax rate, at least. IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Video Contest Is Now Live Of course, the poppy and frenetic “ How to Rob a Bank ” wouldn’t dare to take aim at massive corporations that widen the wealth gap by destroying small businesses, normalizing exploitative labor practices, and accelerating worldwide environmental collapse. This is very specifically a film about how banks are bad and should be fucked with, an opinion that the founder of Amazon might actually share with the average ticket-buyer. And it’s not like the director of “ Bullet Train ” suddenly made a serious call to action that’s poised to inspire a wave of copycat robberies.
